fields.acceptance: A testscript writes a change set whose three leaves link depends-on in a chain, sees change show list them in that order, and has a fourth link closing the loop refused with nothing written.
fields.statement: A change set's leaves link depends-on each other to say which must be built first: the links never form a loop, and the leaves read back in an order that respects them.

fields.acceptance: A testscript links a depends-on b and b depends-on c, then c depends-on a by rhiza link and by rhiza apply: both exit 3 with the loop named and the log entry count unchanged. A Go check test folds a loop made by two concurrent change sets and gets one fail finding on rule depends-on naming the three capabilities.
fields.statement: depends-on between capabilities never forms a loop, as between change sets: rhiza link and rhiza apply refuse a depends-on that would close one, and rhiza check fails on each loop already in the log.

fields.acceptance: A testscript adds leaves c, b and a in that order with c depends-on b and b depends-on a; change show --json lists a, b, c with b's needs [a] and c's needs [b]; leaves with no links come out in tree order; describe-golden is regenerated for the new response field.
fields.statement: rhiza change show --json lists the change set's leaves (the capabilities it adds that have no live children) in build order: each leaf after every leaf it depends-on, ties in tree order, each with the handles it depends on.

fields.acceptance: rhiza guide apply contains a recipe with a depends-on link between two capabilities, the guide tests pass, and the topic stays within its size cap.
fields.statement: rhiza guide apply shows how to link one leaf depends-on another, only where the dependency is real, and says a loop is refused.

fields.acceptance: A testscript in a git repo has a builder commit a leaf's code and then write Evidence that verifies it: rhiza check --json exits 0 with one evidence-actor warning; written by a different actor, there is none.
fields.statement: Evidence names the actor that wrote it, and rhiza check warns when that actor also wrote the code of the leaf the Evidence verifies.

fields.acceptance: A testscript writes Evidence with RHIZA_ACTOR=verifier, then sets a field on it as another actor: show --json still gives actor verifier, and the rendered page under .rhiza/rendered/ names verifier.
fields.statement: An Evidence node's actor is the actor stamped on the log entry that created it: rhiza show --json gives it as actor on every Evidence node, and the rendered Evidence page names it. No field can set or change it.

fields.acceptance: rhiza guide shows the Actor: trailer beside Change: in its commit example and the guide tests pass within the size cap; the run-ship-change testscript finds Actor: with the run's actor on ship's land commit.
fields.statement: Every commit that carries a change set's Change: trailer also carries an Actor: trailer naming the actor that made it: the guide tells agents to add it from RHIZA_ACTOR, which every launched agent has, and the commits rhiza makes itself carry it.

fields.acceptance: A testscript in a git repo commits with Change: <id> and Actor: builder, then writes Evidence verifying the change set's leaf: as builder, check --json exits 0 with one warn finding on rule evidence-actor naming the four; as verifier, no such finding; a commit with no Actor: trailer yields none. Go tests run the rule on given commit trailers, so check itself still runs no git.
fields.statement: rhiza check warns, on a rule named evidence-actor, for each live Evidence that verifies a capability when the Evidence's actor is named in an Actor: trailer of a commit carrying the Change: trailer of the change set that added that capability. The warning names the Evidence, the capability, the actor and the commit. Outside a git work tree the rule is skipped.
Does each build commit name the leaf it builds (a Leaf: trailer, say), so the evidence-actor warning compares only that leaf's commits rather than every commit of the leaf's change set?

ops.note: Until it is settled the warning works per change set: an actor that committed any of the change set's code is warned about as the verifier of any of its leaves.
